property_summary: After any Put call, the sum of balances across all users must equal the total Ether received via Put, but in the mutant a user's balance is not incremented while the contract still receives the Ether, breaking the invariant.
For any account, after a successful Put call with a positive msg.value, the account's balance must increase by exactly msg.value; the mutant performs no increment, so the balance stays unchanged.

For any Put call with positive msg.value, the contract's total ETH balance must grow by msg.value and the sender's recorded balance by msg.value; the mutant omits the balance increase so address(c).balance exceeds the sum of all Acc balances.

After a Put call with a positive msg.value, the sum of all account balances plus the current contract ETH balance must equal 2× the total ETH ever deposited via Put; the mutant omits the balance increment, so the left side becomes 1× total deposits plus current balance, breaking the invariant.

After a successful Put with msg.value > 0, the contract ETH balance increases but the sender's Acc balance does not increase in the mutant, so address(c).balance > sum of all Acc balances across all accounts, which never happens in the original contract.

For any caller, after Put, the caller's balance in Acc must have increased by at least msg.value (i.e., the addition did not silently overflow). The mutant with require(true) removes the overflow check, so a large msg.value combined with a large initial balance can cause an overflow that is not detected, resulting in a balance smaller than expected.

After Put, the sum of all Acc balances equals the total Ether sent to the contract, because the original requires no overflow; the mutant with require(true) can allow an overflow that breaks this conservation, causing total recorded balance to not match total received Ether.

For any sender and any unlock time, after Put(msg.value > 0), the recipient's Acc balance must equal the sum of its previous balance and msg.value, because the original require ensures no overflow; the mutant with require(true) lets overflow wrap the balance, breaking the addition invariant for large enough values.

For any sender with an existing balance, after Put, calling Collect for the full balance must leave the sender's balance at zero; the mutant can cause an overflow in Put that increases the balance beyond uint256 range, making full collection impossible because the balance becomes inconsistent.

For any sender and any _unlockTime parameter, calling Put(...) must set the sender's unlockTime to either the provided _unlockTime (if in the future) or block.timestamp (if _unlockTime is in the past); the buggy version ignores _unlockTime and always uses block.timestamp, violating the rule whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After a call to Put(uint _unlockTime) by any sender with any value, the sender's unlockTime must equal _unlockTime if _unlockTime > block.timestamp, and block.timestamp otherwise; the buggy version violates this for any _unlockTime strictly greater than block.timestamp.

For any sender and _unlockTime > block.timestamp, after Put(_unlockTime), the sender's unlockTime must be greater than block.timestamp; the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, so unlockTime equals block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime strictly greater than block.timestamp, after Put(_unlockTime) the caller's unlockTime must be strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the time of the Put; the buggy version always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, so unlockTime equals block.timestamp.

In the correct contract C, calling Put always fully processes the payment and logs a message, unless the caller would be left with zero balance after an overflow revert; in the mutant, Put's logging can be skipped when a revert occurs inside the assignment (or subsequent code) after the require is removed, so the logged messages differ.

After any call to Put, the caller's Acc balance correctly reflects the sum of msg.value sent, while the mutant may allow an overflow-reverted balance update that leaves the balance unchanged, violating the invariant that balance increases by msg.value.

For any caller and any call to Put, the caller's Acc balance after the call must equal the previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant can leave the balance unchanged when an overflow-triggered revert skips only the failed assignment.

After any Put call, the caller's Acc.balance is exactly the previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant can complete with a lower balance when msg.value causes an overflow revert that is caught inside the function.
After any Put call, the Log contract's last message sender must match the Put caller; the mutant omits the AddMessage call so the last message is not updated.
After a Put call, the History length of the Log contract increases by exactly one; the mutant omits AddMessage so the length does not increase.

After a successful Put, the Log contract's History must be non-empty and its last entry must reflect the Put parameters; the mutant omits the LogFile.AddMessage call, so the History length remains zero for the first Put from an address.
When msg.value is non-zero, the correct Put succeeds and increases the caller's balance, while the buggy Put consistently reverts due to require(false).
For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put should not revert; the buggy version with require(false) always reverts.
For any caller with a non-zero msg.value, calling Put should succeed and not revert; the buggy version with require(false) always reverts, so the call's return status differs.
After any call to Put with any msg.value and any unlock time, the caller's Acc balance must have increased by exactly msg.value; the buggy Put reverts for all inputs, leaving the balance unchanged.

For any caller with zero msg.value, calling Put must complete without reverting, update the caller's unlockTime, and emit a log via LogFile; the buggy require(false) causes a revert even when no value is at stake, so the call's success status and the resulting state changes differ.
A call to Put must add msg.value to the caller's existing balance; the bug replaces the balance with msg.value, so after two different-value Puts the final balance will be wrong.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the caller's balance must be at least the sum of all msg.values sent, because the reference accumulates; the bug overwrites, making the balance less than the sum for some sequence the fuzzer finds.
After two Puts with non-zero values by the same caller, the final balance must equal the sum of the values sent because the reference accumulates; the bug overwrites with only the second value.

After any call to Put, the caller's balance must be >= msg.value; the bug sets balance to exactly msg.value so it holds, but for two calls with different non-zero values the second call's balance will be < the sum, which can be tested indirectly by requiring that a subsequent Collect of the first call's value reverts in the original (balance too low after overwrite) but succeeds in the buggy version after only the second Put if it overwrote.

After any two Put calls by the same caller with different non-zero amounts, the reference's Acc[caller].balance equals the sum of the two msg.values, enabling a subsequent Collect of the first amount to succeed without reverting; the bug overwrites balance with the second msg.value, causing the Collect of the first amount to revert.
After calling Put, the unlockTime stored in Acc[caller] must be >= block.timestamp at the time of the Put call; the buggy version can set it to a value strictly less than block.timestamp.

After Put sets an unlockTime, a subsequent Collect that sends ether should only succeed when the caller's unlockTime is before the current block.timestamp; the buggy version allows a future unlockTime to be overwritten with a past one, making funds withdrawable earlier than intended.

After a Put call resets a holder's unlockTime, subsequent time-dependent operations should be governed by that value, but the buggy version allows Put to assign an arbitrarily small unlockTime regardless of the current block.timestamp, making Collect succeed earlier than intended.
After a Put call, the unlockTime in the caller's Acc must be at least block.timestamp at the time of the Put call; the buggy version can set it lower.
After a Put call, the holder's unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp at call time; the buggy version can set it to _unlockTime which may be strictly less, violating the invariant.
After any number of Put calls, the balance of a holder must be greater than or equal to the sum of msg.value they sent; the buggy subtraction makes balance decrease instead, violating this invariant.

For any two Put calls by the same sender with the same unlockTime and arbitrary msg.values, the final holder balance equals the sum of msg.values sent; the buggy subtraction leads to a balance less than the total sent.
After a single Put call via the fallback, the holder's balance must equal the received msg.value; the buggy subtraction makes the balance equal 0 instead, violating the equality.

After two Put calls of possibly different values by the same sender, the holder's balance must be the sum of the two received Ether amounts; the buggy subtraction reduces the balance instead of increasing it, so after two calls the balance is less than the total sent.

After any number of Put calls, the holder's balance is exactly the sum of all msg.value sent, increased by previous balance. The buggy subtraction makes the balance smaller than the total sent, so for any single Put the holder's balance changes by exactly msg.value according to the reference, while the bug changes it by -msg.value.

After any sequence of Put and Collect calls, the sum of balances across all Acc holders plus the contract's own balance equals the total msg.value received minus MinSum collected, but the mutant fails this because it never records the deposited Ether in acc.balance.

After any Put call, the balance recorded for msg.sender in c.Acc equals the sum of all msg.value previously deposited by that sender via Put; the mutant fails this because it never increments acc.balance.

After a Put call, the contract's total ETH balance should increase by exactly msg.value, but the mutant fails because it never records the deposited Ether in acc.balance, causing a discrepancy between the contract's balance and the sum of all acc.balance entries.
For any address that calls Put, after the call the contract's ETH balance must be strictly greater than before the call, which the mutant violates because it omits the balance increment.
After a Put call, the caller's recorded balance in c.Acc must increase by exactly msg.value; the mutant violates this because it skips the balance increment, so the recorded balance does not change.
After any call to Put, the unlockTime for that sender MUST be at least block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves it unassigned (default 0), so it is not >= block.timestamp.

After a call to Put(uint) by a sender, the unlockTime associated with that sender in the Acc mapping must be strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the time of the original Put call; the buggy version omits the assignment, leaving unlockTime unchanged and potentially less than or equal to the block.timestamp of a previous Put, which a subsequent valid Collect will then rely upon incorrectly.

After a Put call by a sender, the unlockTime must equal the _unlockTime argument if that argument is larger than the current block.timestamp; the buggy version skips the assignment, leaving unlockTime unchanged.

After any successful Put, the sender's unlockTime must equal the block.timestamp at the time of that Put call when the argument is less than or equal to block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves unlockTime unchanged, failing to advance it to the current block.timestamp.

For any sender, after a Put with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, a subsequent Put with _unlockTime <= block.timestamp within the same timestamp must set unlockTime to block.timestamp; the buggy version leaves it at the old future time, breaking the invariant that unlockTime never exceeds block.timestamp after a Put with a past-or-present argument.
After any `Put` call, the `LastMsg.Sender` property in the `Log` contract should reflect `msg.sender`; the buggy variant logs `address(0)` instead.
After a successful Put, the History array in the Log contract must contain a message whose Sender matches the caller that performed the Put; the buggy version logs address(0) instead.
After any Put call, the Acc balance of the caller increases by msg.value; the buggy version does not alter this balance correctly for some inputs.
After a Put call, the History array length in the Log contract increases by exactly 1 and its last entry's Sender equals the caller; the buggy version logs address(0) instead.

For any caller and any unlock time, after calling Put with some ETH, the LogFile's last message should record the actual msg.value sent; the bug records 0 instead, breaking the invariant that the logged value matches the payment.
After a successful Put, the LogFile's last added message should have a Val equal to the Ether sent in the call; the bug uses 0 instead, so for any non-zero send the invariant breaks.

For any call to Put with non-zero Ether, the sender's Acc balance must equal the sum of Val fields in all History messages added by that sender; the mutant records 0 instead of msg.value, so the sum of logged values becomes less than the balance for any non-zero deposit, breaking the invariant.

After any call to Put, the sum of Val fields across all messages in LogFile's History must equal the total Ether deposited (address(c).balance minus initial setup) because the correct contract logs exact msg.value; the mutant logs 0 instead, causing a mismatch for any non-zero deposit.

After any call to Put with any non-zero Ether, the Val of the last Message in LogFile's History must equal the msg.value sent; the mutant records 0, so the last message's Val differs from the sent amount.

The reference C never allows a Collect to succeed when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime; the buggy C allows Collect to succeed even when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime, causing premature withdrawals.

For any account that has previously Put funds, a successful Collect call under the buggy version can reduce the account's balance while the same call under the reference version would revert due to the unlock time not having passed, leading to a mismatch in the account's balance.

After a call to Collect(am) returns, if msg.sender has an unlockTime set in the future relative to the current block timestamp, the reference C must never allow a successful withdrawal (balance reduction), whereas the buggy version may allow it.

For any caller who has deposited, while block.timestamp <= unlockTime, a call to Collect that would succeed in the buggy contract due to the missing time condition must fail in the reference contract, so the caller's balance cannot decrease before the unlock time.

For any caller, a Collect call that does not revert must leave the caller's balance reduced only if block.timestamp > caller's unlockTime; the buggy version can reduce the balance even before the unlock time passes.

For any caller with a positive balance less than MinSum, a Collect call that otherwise succeeds should revert due to the MinSum check; the bug removes this check, allowing collection to succeed and draining the balance.
After any Collect call not triggered by a fallback, if the caller's balance is less than MinSum, the call must revert in the reference; the mutant allows it to succeed and drain the balance.

For any caller who has a nonzero balance strictly below MinSum and a future unlockTime, attempt to collect any positive amount ≤ balance must revert in the reference; the mutant allows the collection to succeed leaving the caller with a lower balance.
For any caller with balance < MinSum, after any Collect the caller's balance must remain unchanged; the mutant allows a non-reverting Collect that reduces the caller's balance below MinSum.

For any caller with a balance strictly less than MinSum, invoking Collect with a positive amount must always revert; the mutant, lacking the MinSum guard, allows a successful collection that decreases the caller's balance.
After Collect, the caller's Acc balance in the reference contract never exceeds their balance before the call, but the mutant's addition makes it strictly increase.

After a successful Collect, the contract's total Ether balance decreases by exactly the collected amount in the reference, but the mutant's addition to acc.balance can cause subsequent Collects to drain more Ether than the contract holds, breaking the invariant that address(c).balance >= sum of all Acc balances.

The sum of all holders' stored balances never exceeds the contract's ETH balance in the reference, but the mutant's addition on Collect inflates stored balances without increasing ETH, so a subsequent collect by a second holder can attempt to transfer more ETH than the contract holds, causing the call to revert.

In the reference, a successful Collect does not change the contract's ETH balance because the caller is already credited for the sent amount, whereas the mutant's addition to acc.balance allows a subsequent Collect by a different holder to transfer more ETH than the contract holds, causing a revert.

In the reference, a successful Collect strictly decreases the contract's ETH balance; in the mutant, because the internal balance is instead increased, a subsequent Collect by the same holder can transfer out enough ETH to leave the contract with less ETH than the total internal balances, violating the invariant that address(c).balance >= sum of all Acc balances.

The external ETH balance of contract C should never decrease after a successful Collect call when the caller is a regular EOA, but the mutant's self-call causes a net balance reduction because the sent ETH remains inside C while the caller's accounting is still deducted.

After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must decrease by exactly _am and contract's ETH balance must reflect the outgoing value, but the mutant sends ETH to itself so the contract's ETH balance does not decrease while the internal balance is still deducted.

After a successful Collect, the ETH balance of contract C must decrease by exactly _am, but the mutant sends ETH to itself so the contract's ETH balance does not decrease while the internal balance is still deducted.

After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must decrease by exactly _am while the contract's ETH balance must decrease by exactly _am, but the mutant sends ETH to itself so the contract's ETH balance does not decrease while the internal balance is still deducted.

After a successful Collect, the ETH balance of contract C must decrease by exactly the collected amount because funds are sent externally, but the mutant sends ETH to itself so the contract's ETH balance remains unchanged.
